content.p: Jamell Demons, who records as YNW Melly, has been in a Florida jail since February 2019, accused of shooting two of his closest friends dead. He has pleaded not guilty and has never been convicted. His first trial, in Broward County in the summer of 2023, ended without a verdict when the jury deadlocked. Prosecutors chose to try him again, and the retrial is now set for January 2027, roughly eight years after his arrest.

The victims were Anthony Williams and Christopher Thomas Jr., fellow members of the YNW rap collective, known as YNW Sakchaser and YNW Juvy. Prosecutors say Demons killed them inside a Jeep after a late-night recording session and then staged the scene to look like a drive-by shooting. His lawyers have stressed that the gun was never recovered and that there was no apparent motive. In between the two trials the case has produced a removed prosecutor, thrown-out evidence, a plea deal for the co-defendant, and a string of witness-tampering charges that were later dropped.

According to prosecutors, the four members of the collective spent the hours up to the early morning of 26 October 2018 at a recording studio in Fort Lauderdale: Demons, Williams, Thomas and Cortlen Henry, who performs as YNW Bortlen. They left together in a Jeep that Henry was driving. NBC 6 South Florida reported that the victims were 21 and 19.

The Sun Sentinel reported that, in the state's account, Demons sat behind Henry. Pitchfork, citing Miramar police, said Williams and Thomas were last seen around 3:20 a.m. in Fort Lauderdale and reached Memorial Hospital Miramar at roughly 4:35 a.m. shot several times, as police described it. A police spokesperson said the two were already dead. The Broward Palm Beach New Times reported that someone left the two men outside the hospital in a Jeep Compass just before 5 a.m.

Henry told police that the group had been the target of a drive-by shooter. Prosecutors reject that account. In their version, as the Sun Sentinel and AP reported it, Demons and Henry stopped in an isolated area and fired at the Jeep from the outside to stage the scene, and Henry then drove the two bodies to the hospital alone. Ballistics evidence, prosecutors say, shows the fatal shots came from inside the vehicle.

Miramar police announced the arrests of Demons and Henry on Wednesday 13 February 2019. Each was charged with two counts of first-degree murder. In its statement, the department said an investigation supported by forensic evidence had concluded that Demons shot and killed the two men and that he and Henry staged the crime scene to resemble a drive-by. Police believed Henry was the driver. Demons, then 19, turned himself in the same day. In an Instagram post he wrote that a lot of rumours and lies were being said, and he called Williams and Thomas his brothers.

The arrest came a month after the release of a mixtape that included a track with Kanye West, and just as the rapper's career was taking off, according to the New Times. Public court documents summarised by Pitchfork added detail to the case. Police cited phone records they said placed Demons at the scene, and they cited autopsy reports and crime-scene details that they said showed he fired from inside the car. They argued that the bullet holes on the outside of the vehicle were made to misdirect the investigation.

Prosecutors also filed notice that they would seek the death penalty. That decision became a legal fight of its own. According to Billboard, Florida requires such notice within 45 days of arraignment, and the state had given it when it first indicted him in 2019 but not after a superseding indictment. A trial judge ruled in July 2022 that the state had lost the chance to seek death. An appeals court reversed that in November 2022, writing that "notice is notice", and the state urged the Florida Supreme Court in 2023 to decline Demons' appeal.
Judge John Murphy presided over the trial, which Pitchfork's timeline said ran for more than a month before the prosecution rested. NBC 6 counted 19 days of argument before deliberations began.

The state's case, as the Sun Sentinel summarised it, was that Demons was seen on surveillance footage getting into the seat from which forensic experts say the gunman fired, and that he told investigators the victims died in a drive-by even though the bullets came from inside the car. Pitchfork's trial timeline noted that a medical examiner testified that Williams was shot multiple times after a shot to the back of the head, and that the state called the lead detective, Mark Moretti, who was on the stand for more than a week. The state's witnesses also included a Broward Sheriff's Office firearms expert and Treveon Glass, who had been at the studio with the group.

The defence told jurors that the gun was never recovered and that Demons had no apparent motive, as AP reported. NBC 6 reported that the defence maintained Demons was at home sleeping at the time and claimed Henry was responsible. Prosecutors argued the killings were gang-related and that Demons had tangled with the victims over money and creative credit, according to the Sun Sentinel; defence lawyers said the gang claim lacked credibility because the men were close friends. Demons did not testify. Pitchfork reported that the defence called one witness, a friend named Adrian Green.

Closing arguments ended on a Thursday in July 2023. The jury told the judge on Friday it was deadlocked, received the standard instruction to keep trying, and on Saturday 22 July asked to see the damaged phone of Christopher Thomas before announcing it could not agree. Murphy declared a mistrial. The Sun Sentinel counted more than 14 hours of deliberation across three days; NBC 6 counted two days. Attorneys later told NBC 6 that one juror who favoured Demons refused to convict and persuaded two others to vote not guilty. Thomas's mother wrote on Facebook after the mistrial that her son was dead "for no reason".
content.h2: The long road to a second trial
content.p: A retrial was first set for early October 2023, but the case soon went sideways. According to the Miami Herald, Murphy removed prosecutor Kristine Bradley from the case after the defence said it would call her as a witness, a dispute tied to allegations about the lead detective, Mark Moretti. A new team arrived, including Alixandra Buckelew, who had co-prosecuted the three men convicted of killing the rapper XXXTentacion. The new team added dozens of witnesses and a list of 58 of Demons' songs it wanted to play, arguing they were his own words.

In the week the retrial was due to begin, prosecutors filed new witness-tampering charges. XXL reported that the state accused Demons and Henry of conspiring to keep Demons' former girlfriend, Mariah Hamilton, from testifying at the first trial. The Herald described a jail scheme of code words and false names, in which inmate Terrence Mathis told Henry to speak to "Rihanna" and "A$AP Rocky's baby mama"; investigators read this as an instruction to keep Hamilton from testifying.

On 20 December 2023 Murphy threw out a large body of digital evidence from Demons' phone, email and social media accounts, confining most of it to the day of and the time following the killings. XXL reported that the state appealed to the Fourth District Court of Appeal, and the case stood still. NBC 6 reported that a promotional video about Demons' life was also suppressed. Henry's own case stalled with it.

Judge Martin Fein, who inherited the case, said in July 2025 that jury selection would still begin on 10 September, over the state's objection that the appeals court had not ruled, the Sun Sentinel reported. In August the appeals court granted a stay, and on 8 August 2025 Fein moved the retrial to January 2027, according to the Sun Sentinel. The Sun Sentinel also described accusations of misconduct from both sides: the defence accused prosecutors of plotting to hide key information, and prosecutors accused Demons, and possibly one of his lawyers, of witness tampering.

Henry, who faced two first-degree murder counts, accepted a deal on 9 September 2025, the day before his own trial was to start, NBC 6 reported. He pleaded no contest to two counts of accessory after the fact, and the judge adjudicated him guilty of them. WQCS reported that the deal also covered two witness-tampering counts, and Vibe's account of the charges lists tampering and unlawful use of a two-way communication device among them. The murder charges were dropped. He was sentenced to a decade in prison, then six years of probation, with time already served counted toward it. WQCS said an initial offer on 4 September had carried 16 years.

Prosecutors cited his lack of prior criminal history and insufficient evidence, according to court documents quoted by WQCS. Fein told him: "I'm not quite sure how your lawyers managed to do this, but I wish you good luck, sir." Henry must give prosecutors a sworn statement about his role, and his lawyers said he would not be required to testify against Demons. Henry's attorney Joe Nascimento pointed out that a no-contest plea means he "hasn't really admitted anything".

On 5 January 2026 Demons was in court as both sides filed motions on what a new jury could hear. Local 10 reported that his witness-tampering trial was set for 21 January. Instead, Rolling Stone reported on 20 January that prosecutors had dismissed all four tampering-related charges, a day before jury selection was due to start. The counts were witness tampering, running a criminal gang, soliciting murder, and conspiring to tamper with a witness in a capital case. His new lawyers, Drew Findling and Carey Haughwout, said the state had taken 652 days to conclude what they said had been obvious: that no crimes had occurred.

The lawyers then pressed for his release. At a four-hour hearing on 30 April 2026, the defence argued that Demons had been jailed for seven years without a conviction and proposed a home in Broward County with 24-hour supervision, cameras and no social media. Family members testified, as did a Broward Sheriff's Office officer, Maj. Kevin Corbett, who described Demons' conditions in custody. Prosecutors answered that he has an open dorm to himself with a shower, television and basketball court, and read a letter they said he had written from jail: "It's like a mansion."

Fein denied bond in a 39-page order filed on 6 May 2026, Hot97 reported. He wrote that the state's evidence was "arguably sufficient to convict", and cited the standard for denying bond in capital cases. The order did not adopt an earlier finding that Demons was affiliated with violent gangs. Demons' lawyers called the conditions he has endured "inhumane", said he remains innocent in the eyes of the law, and said that only "a jury's verdict" now appears likely to end his confinement.

Demons still faces two counts of first-degree murder, with the death penalty available if he is convicted. Reporting by the Miami Herald noted that the case would fall under Florida's rule allowing a death recommendation on an 8 to 4 jury vote. The retrial is expected in January 2027. What a new jury will be allowed to hear is still partly unsettled: the digital evidence limits, the status of the songs the state wants to introduce and the question of whether Henry will be called all bear on how the second trial will differ from the first. Prosecutors have said the state's evidence points to Demons as the shooter, and Demons' lawyers say the state failed to win a conviction once and will fail again.
